quote: “There is always something left to love. And if you ain’t learned that, you ain’t learned nothing.”
source: Lorraine Hansberry, A Raisin in the Sun, Act III (Random House, 1959) (Mama, Lena Younger)
speaker: Mama (Lena Younger)

evidence.where: PBS American Masters, eight quotations from the play, giving the line verbatim to Mama in Act III; the Act III text at americanliterature.com confirms the exchange with Beneatha
evidence.edition: A Raisin in the Sun (Random House, 1959)
evidence.locator: Act III, Mama to Beneatha, after Beneatha says there is nothing left to love in Walter

reason: Mama says exactly this to Beneatha in Act III, answering her daughter’s refusal to love her brother; the wording matches the published play. Not shipped, not at cap, not banned.
